The '''Battle of Migov''' was a 1949-1952 urban battle during the [[Nogoyevian War of Independence]]. It was fought for [[Migov]], the capital and cultural center of Nogoyev.

The battle became one of the bloodiest events of the war. The source describes slow, block-by-block fighting, heavy artillery and airstrikes, fortified buildings, mines, snipers, and severe civilian hardship.

== Course ==

Zhensanovian forces attempted to take Migov as a decisive strategic and symbolic target. Nogoyevian defenders used the city itself as a defensive system, fighting from buildings, tunnels, barricades, and improvised strongpoints.

The battle lasted three years. In 1952, a major Nogoyevian offensive forced exhausted Union forces to retreat from the city.

== Legacy ==

Migov became the central symbol of Nogoyevian resistance. The source describes the raising of a Nogoyevian flag at the destroyed western edge of the city as the iconic image of the victory.

The casualty figure in the source is extremely high and should be checked before final publication. For now, the draft preserves it as a source claim rather than a final audited number.
